- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to match sentiment reversal.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days), especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish — cap forecast peak at 1-2% below true peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-forecasting in early horizon when price is trending up, under-forecasting when trending down — adjust for recent 5-day average if sentiment is flat.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1-3% in bullish sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.67 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.33) or recent sentiment is mixed, model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.0 point to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
